from pathlib import Path
Path("analysis/review.md").write_text("# Final review

The review retains all 29 baseline findings and their original questions, appends N01–N07, and records nine qualifications and 11 precise test bindings in the supplement. The original rows are historical evidence. The qualifications narrow their scope where timing, hook behavior, or receiver identity mattered. [Final findings](final.json) · [Supplement](supplement.json) · [Original open questions](../baseline/open-questions.md)

## Identity and ordered effects

- **N01 and F22.** A shallow copy of wrapper W initially shares W's inner breaker A. A new admission through either copy affects A while both point to it. An overwrite of a separate copy or a rebind of the caller's local pointer leaves W intact. A retained callback still reads W. Overwriting W itself changes the pointer the callback will read. [Wrapper field and constructor](../gobreaker.go#L133-L138) · [Admission and callback](../gobreaker.go#L265-L273)
- **N02.** During A's admission, its half-open notification overwrites W with B. The already-entered `beforeRequest` still increments A's admission counter and unlocks A. The generation sent back to Allow belongs to A, but the returned callback reads W at invocation. Both A and B have independently reached half-open and their numeric generations match. B has no admissions and closes on the redirected success with `MaxRequests=1`. A remains half-open with a full slot. Restoring W lets the same callback close A. This establishes a case where the targets already differ when Allow returns. [Admission and unlock](../gobreaker.go#L265-L290) · [Comparison and success threshold](../gobreaker.go#L293-L318)
- **N03 and F07/F08/F22.** A callback from A, invoked through an overwritten W on expired-open B, runs B's lifecycle resolution and notifies with B's name before rejecting the report at the generation check. The false result contributes no failure and A stays pending. The preserved F22 mismatch probe holds B unexpired and therefore observes B stay open. F08 requires a configured notification, and the comparison follows it only when it returns normally. F19 covers the panic path on the original receiver. [Completion ordering](../gobreaker.go#L293-L307) · [Expiry and notification](../gobreaker.go#L334-L360)
- **N04.** A stored `Execute` method value binds the pointer when it is formed. In ordinary execution, A receives admission, classifies the result with A's stored function, and accounts on A before returning the original pair. In the request-panic path, A receives the deferred failure report and releases its report lock, and the original panic reaches the caller when reporting returns normally. The tests cover a local pointer rebind before invocation and a rebind inside the panicking request. B stays untouched. [Execute receiver, admission, ordinary and panic paths](../gobreaker.go#L228-L245) · [Reporting lock](../gobreaker.go#L293-L307)
- **N05.** Construction stores callback function values from Settings. Reassigning the caller's Settings field leaves the stored callback in use. Its closure can still see changes to captured application state. The probe specifically checks IsSuccessful. ReadyToTrip and OnStateChange use the same constructor storage pattern. ReadyToTrip receives a Counts value, and OnStateChange receives the selected breaker's name and transition state values. [Settings storage](../gobreaker.go#L140-L175) · [Classifier use](../gobreaker.go#L242-L244) · [Trip hook](../gobreaker.go#L322-L331) · [Notification](../gobreaker.go#L348-L360)
- **N06.** Overwriting W with a zero wrapper causes a retained callback to panic at the nil inner receiver before it compares generations. A survives through its alias. Restore W and the retained callback can report to A. The probe recovers a panic without matching runtime-specific panic text. The constructor is documented. The lifetime after whole-wrapper replacement is silent. [Wrapper and constructor](../gobreaker.go#L133-L138) · [Constructor initialization](../gobreaker.go#L182-L187) · [Dereference during report](../gobreaker.go#L265-L299)
- **N07 and F15/F16/F19/F20.** Each report fixes its inner receiver for the duration of that report. A's trip hook overwrites W with B and panics after A's failure count has been updated. A's deferred unlock executes and a public Counts read of A returns the partial charge. B stays untouched until a manual retry re-reads W, finds B's matching generation, and applies a failure to B with zero admissions there. The same-inner mutex in F20 also applies through wrapper aliases. An independent inner breaker uses its own mutex. The same-inner lock inference remains source-based. [Target lookup](../gobreaker.go#L265-L273) · [Lock and cleanup](../gobreaker.go#L293-L307) · [Failure before hook](../gobreaker.go#L322-L331)

F04's late success closes once the cumulative success threshold is reached. Its preserved probe uses `MaxRequests=1`. F10's original-pair delivery requires normal classification and reporting, including any hook reached during expiry resolution. F16 and F19's manually retried completions use unchanged inner receivers and the stated timing. F20's mutex rule concerns lock-taking calls made from ReadyToTrip or OnStateChange. IsSuccessful runs before afterRequest acquires the mutex. [Success threshold](../gobreaker.go#L310-L319) · [Normal return](../gobreaker.go#L234-L244) · [Hook and lock ordering](../gobreaker.go#L293-L327)

## Flash draft dispositions

All 21 claim citations matched source text. The draft's Jev pass labeled all of them supported. The dispositions below incorporate the surrounding control flow and the preserved probes. [Draft output](draft-verify.json)

- **C1–C4.** Accept the capture of the numeric value from admission and the later comparison against the selected receiver's current state and generation. C2's generation is the value returned after any lazy transition observed by admission that returns normally. C3 describes the value parameter in afterRequest. The receiver lookup at callback invocation is separate, and the draft omits its consequences under overwrite. [Capture and use](../gobreaker.go#L265-L299)
- **C5–C8.** Accept the mismatch short circuit for outcome accounting and the dispatch of both matched outcomes with the newly resolved state. Qualify C5 and C6 with currentState and its potential state changes, count clearing and notification before comparison. [Report order](../gobreaker.go#L293-L307) · [Expiry and notification](../gobreaker.go#L334-L360)
- **C9–C12.** Accept the branches on the selected receiver. C9's success updates total and consecutive successes and resets consecutive failures. C10's close condition is at least MaxRequests and does not check Requests in that branch. C11 receives the post-increment Counts by value. C12 reopens directly and clears through the transition. [Success counters](../gobreaker.go#L59-L63) · [Outcome branches](../gobreaker.go#L310-L331) · [Generation reset](../gobreaker.go#L348-L365)
- **C13–C14.** Accept the same-state early return specifically in setState. A closed interval can advance the generation with no state change. A generation increment invalidates the immediately preceding value on that same receiver; an old value can compare equal on a distinct breaker, and F29 retains the theoretical full-wrap limit. [Closed interval](../gobreaker.go#L334-L339) · [Set and increment](../gobreaker.go#L348-L365)
- **C15–C18.** Accept Execute's local generation, stable receiver, and ordinary classification. C17's false is an attempted failure report for a non-nil recovered panic after admission. That report may be stale. C18's propagation of the same panic requires the report to return normally. F14 and F17 preserve the cases where a later reporting panic takes precedence. Admission occurs before the defer is installed, and F21 preserves termination without a panic. [Execute](../gobreaker.go#L228-L245) · [Admission and reporting](../gobreaker.go#L276-L307)
- **C19–C21.** Accept the notification after commit and under the inner breaker's lock on public paths, with C20's nil guard. Accept C21 for matching closed failure; stale outcomes never dispatch to ReadyToTrip and half-open failure reopens directly. [Public State](../gobreaker.go#L205-L213) · [Admission and reporting locks](../gobreaker.go#L276-L307) · [Hooks and reset](../gobreaker.go#L322-L365)

### Draft questions

- **Q1.** README specifies discarding counts from requests sent before clearing on the same breaker. F07–F09 retain questions beyond that count guarantee. Q1 supplies no exemption for a particular admission state. [README count contract](../README.md#L77-L79) · [Generation check](../gobreaker.go#L293-L307)
- **Q2.** On one breaker, whichever locked operation advances the generation first affects later comparison, and F28 retains the scheduling issue for panic fallback. Across replacement, the selected receiver and expiry processing also matter. The broader ordering contract stays open. [Report and mutex](../gobreaker.go#L293-L307)
- **Q3.** A closed-interval reset advances the generation before comparing, so a formerly matching value can be discarded on the same breaker. Replacement selects a distinct receiver and that receiver can have a matching number. F09 and F22 cover the separate cases. [Comparison](../gobreaker.go#L293-L307) · [Interval reset](../gobreaker.go#L334-L345)
- **Q4–Q6.** Both Execute paths use the same report guard. A request panic bypasses classification, a classifier panic enters failure reporting, and trip/notification panics have the existing accounting and retry consequences. README's panic wording addresses the request itself. Hook eligibility, panic precedence, and stale side effects stay open under F10–F19. [README Execute contract](../README.md#L81-L91) · [Execute implementation](../gobreaker.go#L228-L245)
- **Q7.** F20 keeps synchronous re-entry open. The lock is attached to the selected inner breaker and alias wrappers can lead back to it. No deadlock was staged. [Report lock](../gobreaker.go#L293-L307) · [Notification invocation](../gobreaker.go#L348-L360)
- **Q8.** The implementation installs state and advances generation before the nil check. A returning no-op callback does not add generation changes of its own. The call still runs synchronously under the lock if present. This is a code observation and supplies no general equivalence guarantee about timing. [Commit and guard](../gobreaker.go#L348-L365)
- **Q9.** The fresh closed failure charges counts before the hook. Settings documents the Counts argument as a copy, so the hook receives a value snapshot of the charged receiver. [Documented callback argument](../gobreaker.go#L95-L98) · [Charge and invocation](../gobreaker.go#L322-L327)
- **Q10.** The same-state early return concerns one setState call on one object. The F22 target is a separate constructed object. Its matching initial number did not result from an unchanged-state call. [Construction](../gobreaker.go#L140-L186) · [Set and increment](../gobreaker.go#L348-L365)
- **Q11–Q12.** Source shows wrapper overwrite selects another object. The numeric comparison applies to the resolved state of that object and does not compare admission receiver identity or admission state. N01–N03 and N07 probe the difference. The contract for replacement and retained callbacks stays open. [Allow and dispatch](../gobreaker.go#L265-L307)

## Final Jev batch

The single batch returned one supported proposal (C12, the half-open success threshold), one contradicted proposal (C4), and 12 unclear proposals. C4's proposition is observed directly in N02. B is verified half-open with zero Counts immediately before the call, the callback was obtained from A's admission, and B closes while A still has its sole admission outstanding. The source compares the current generation and increments consecutive successes before comparing that counter with MaxRequests. Requests is only part of admission here. The runtime result and source take precedence over the verdict. [Batch output](final-jev.json) · [C4 probe](./_postprobe/identity_post_test.go) · [Admission and completion logic](../gobreaker.go#L276-L318)

The unclear calls include several statements requiring multiple control-flow sites or Go value semantics. C1–C3 and C5 use the wrapper field, the already-bound admission call, and the callback's new lookup, supported by N01 and N02. N03 establishes C6 with the observed target notification. N04 establishes C7–C8 with distinct hooks and counters. N05 establishes C9–C10 with a stored function and mutable captured flag. C11's nil receiver follows from the wrapper field and the first mutex access, and N06 observed the panic and restored report. C13 remains a source inference from inner receiver locking and wrapper aliasing. N07 establishes C14 with distinct hooks and the observed charges before and after retry. No judgment was resubmitted. The two requested CLI outputs retain the full drafts, questions, and verdict data emitted by those commands. The CLI normalizes successful responses and does not emit a separate raw transport envelope. [Batch inputs](final-checks.json) · [Batch output](final-jev.json) · [Public-seam probes](./_postprobe/identity_post_test.go)

## Probe results and preservation

Both attempts used the requested command.

```sh
go test -race -count=3 -timeout=30s -json -overlay analysis/overlay-final.json -run '^TestIdentity' .
```

- Attempt 1, retained pilot log `033`, passed all 22 preserved and the first six added top-level probes three times. There were 51 discovered subtest names. Both streams are retained, with 952 stdout lines and empty stderr.
- Attempt 2, retained pilot log `088`, also includes the new reporting-hook overwrite and retry probe. All 22 preserved and seven added top-level probes and all 51 subtest names had three run and three pass events each. The package passed in 6.658 seconds. There were no skips, failures, missing tests or race reports. Both streams are retained, with 964 stdout lines and empty stderr.
- `python3 validate_postreview.py` passed in log `091` with 29 retained rows, seven additions, nine qualifications and 11 test bindings. It verifies immutable inputs and overlay preservation, plus finding and citation structure. [Final overlay](overlay-final.json) · [Original overlay](overlay.json)

## Remaining work and limits

The probes exercise sequential wrapper copying and replacement, synchronous hook-driven replacement, caller rebinding, and ordinary concurrent schedules already present in the baseline. Concurrent overwrites of the same wrapper field were outside this review. Copying or overwriting an in-use CircuitBreaker value was also outside scope because it embeds a sync.Mutex, whose contract excludes copying after first use. The public TwoStep wrapper contains only a pointer. README does not describe replacing that wrapper while a completion is retained. The source establishes the current behavior and leaves support and policy open. [Breaker mutex and wrapper field](../gobreaker.go#L116-L138) · [README usage](../README.md#L15-L25) · [Allow contract](../gobreaker.go#L262-L273)

The documented half-open admission cap, count clearing and rejection of old outcomes on the same breaker, copy argument for ReadyToTrip, and request-panic behavior supply the cited contract where applicable. They leave open completion ownership after replacement, the caller's abandonment protocol, exactly-once reporting, hook re-entry and panic precedence. The baseline also leaves exact clock equality, counter capacity, generation wrap, and State-triggered notification panic/retry unprobed. All original questions remain available in their historical wording. [README settings and behavior](../README.md#L39-L91) · [Original open questions](../baseline/open-questions.md)
")
Path("analysis/summary.md").write_text("# Final review summary

All 29 original findings and questions were preserved verbatim by field. Seven findings were appended, and nine historical claims received qualifications in the supplement. The structural and immutable-input checks passed. [Final findings](final.json) · [Supplement](supplement.json)

- `Allow` captures the admitting generation and the outer wrapper pointer. Each invocation looks up the inner breaker again. A separate wrapper copy or caller-local pointer rebind leaves the callback's lookup intact. Overwriting the captured wrapper can redirect the report, including when the overwrite occurs inside the admission hook. [Review and evidence](review.md#identity-and-ordered-effects)
- A redirected success closed a different half-open breaker that had admitted zero requests. A redirected report with a generation mismatch still advanced the selected breaker's elapsed open timeout and delivered its notification before discarding the outcome. A hook that overwrote the wrapper and panicked left its partial charge and unlocked the original receiver, then a manual retry charged the replacement. [Public-seam probes](_postprobe/identity_post_test.go)
- `Execute` retained the originally bound receiver for admission, classification, ordinary accounting and deferred panic reporting across caller-local pointer rebinding. Constructor-stored callbacks also retained their function values while observing changes to their own captured environment. [Source](../gobreaker.go#L140-L175) · [Execute](../gobreaker.go#L228-L245)

The final race run passed 29 top-level probes and 51 subtest names three times each, with zero skips and empty stderr. Both attempts are retained in pilot logs `033` and `088`. Jev's contradiction of the redirected half-open success is recorded alongside the test and source evidence. Wrapper replacement support and every original intent question remain open. [Detailed review](review.md)
")
